content.title: About
content.content: Pinto beans are dried beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) widely used in North and South American cuisines. They have a light‑brown color with speckles and a mild, slightly nutty flavor. Dried beans require soaking and cooking before they can be added to soups, stews, salads, or side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pinto beans are among the most consumed bean varieties in Mexico and the United States.
The name “pinto” comes from the Spanish word for “painted,” referring to the speckled appearance of the beans.
When kept dry and cool, dried beans can be stored for up to a year.
Pinto beans are a good source of complex carbohydrates, providing sustained energy.
They are traditionally used to make “refried beans,” a staple in Mexican cooking.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of dried pinto beans provides about 21 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: Pinto beans contain iron for oxygen transport and magnesium for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: These beans contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Contain antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals such as polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals; thorough soaking and rinsing can help.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to beans, experiencing skin or digestive reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak pinto beans in water for at least 6–8 hours, drain, and then simmer for 1–1.5 hours until tender. Use them in soups, chili, salads, mash them for spreads, or incorporate into vegetarian patties. For a richer flavor, you can briefly sauté the cooked beans.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried pinto beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored, they keep their quality for up to 12 months. Discard beans that develop a moldy odor or show signs of moisture.
